raw.label: basic
raw.prompt:
Run this real Linux provisioning and public-repository build benchmark using your computer tool. You must actually execute all steps; do not merely describe commands. First call computer with op=start (timeoutMs 120000). Then exec ["/bin/bash","-lc","uname -m; nproc; free -m; df -h ~; node --version; npm --version"] and retain output. The working directory is /workspace. Node is preinstalled; if missing install it and record that separately.

Run each of the following as a SEPARATE computer exec call with timeoutMs 1200000 and argv ["/bin/bash","-lc", SHELL]. Use /usr/bin/time -f 'BENCH_WALL_SECONDS=%e' -o /workspace/STEP.time /bin/bash -lc 'COMMAND' > /workspace/STEP.log 2>&1; rc=$?; cat /workspace/STEP.time; tail -n 14 /workspace/STEP.log; exit $rc. This saves full logs without exceeding output limits. Do not combine steps because each time must remain independent:
1. STEP=express-clone COMMAND=cd /workspace && git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/expressjs/express
2. STEP=express-install COMMAND=cd /workspace/express && npm install
3. STEP=express-test COMMAND=cd /workspace/express && npm test
4. STEP=rust-install COMMAND=curl --proto "=https" --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y --profile minimal
5. STEP=ripgrep-clone COMMAND=cd /workspace && git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep
6. STEP=ripgrep-build COMMAND=export PATH=/root/.cargo/bin:$PATH; cd /workspace/ripgrep && cargo build --release

Continue after a failed test, recording its exit code and reason. If installation/build fails, inspect the saved log and resource availability; recover only if a straightforward fix is possible, and time retries separately. If a command might exceed the exec timeout, launch it as a background job writing its exit status and poll every 30 seconds in another exec. Do not change npm scripts or source code, skip tests, reduce the requested release build, or claim completion while jobs are running. Finally run /workspace/ripgrep/target/release/rg --version, git -C /workspace/express rev-parse HEAD, git -C /workspace/ripgrep rev-parse HEAD, du -sb /workspace/ripgrep /workspace/ripgrep/target, and df -h /workspace. Leave the machine running and files intact. Report observed times, exit codes and any recovery; do not snapshot or sleep yet because the benchmark harness measures those next.

Run this real Linux provisioning and public-repository build benchmark using your computer tool. You must actually execute all steps; do not merely describe commands. First call computer with op=start (timeoutMs 120000). Then exec ["/bin/bash","-lc","uname -m; nproc; free -m; df -h ~; node --version; npm --version"] and retain output. The working directory is /workspace. Node is preinstalled; if missing install it and record that separately.

Run each of the following as a SEPARATE computer exec call with timeoutMs 1200000 and argv ["/bin/bash","-lc", SHELL]. Use /usr/bin/time -f 'BENCH_WALL_SECONDS=%e' -o /workspace/STEP.time /bin/bash -lc 'COMMAND' > /workspace/STEP.log 2>&1; rc=$?; cat /workspace/STEP.time; tail -n 14 /workspace/STEP.log; exit $rc. This saves full logs without exceeding output limits. Do not combine steps because each time must remain independent:
1. STEP=express-clone COMMAND=cd /workspace && git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/expressjs/express
2. STEP=express-install COMMAND=cd /workspace/express && npm install
3. STEP=express-test COMMAND=cd /workspace/express && npm test
4. STEP=rust-install COMMAND=curl --proto "=https" --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y --profile minimal
5. STEP=ripgrep-clone COMMAND=cd /workspace && git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep
6. STEP=ripgrep-build COMMAND=export PATH=/root/.cargo/bin:$PATH; cd /workspace/ripgrep && cargo build --release

Continue after a failed test, recording its exit code and reason. If installation/build fails, inspect the saved log and resource availability; recover only if a straightforward fix is possible, and time retries separately. If a command might exceed the exec timeout, launch it as a background job writing its exit status and poll every 30 seconds in another exec. Do not change npm scripts or source code, skip tests, reduce the requested release build, or claim completion while jobs are running. Finally run /workspace/ripgrep/target/release/rg --version, git -C /workspace/express rev-parse HEAD, git -C /workspace/ripgrep rev-parse HEAD, du -sb /workspace/ripgrep /workspace/ripgrep/target, and df -h /workspace. Leave the machine running and files intact. Report observed times, exit codes and any recovery; do not snapshot or sleep yet because the benchmark harness measures those next.

raw.prompt:
Run this real Linux provisioning and public-repository build benchmark using your computer tool. You must actually execute all steps; do not merely describe commands. First call computer with op=start (timeoutMs 120000). Then exec ["/bin/bash","-lc","uname -m; nproc; free -m; df -h ~; node --version; npm --version"] and retain output. The working directory is /workspace. Node is preinstalled; if missing install it and record that separately.

Run each of the following as a SEPARATE computer exec call with timeoutMs 1200000 and argv ["/bin/bash","-lc", SHELL]. Use /usr/bin/time -f 'BENCH_WALL_SECONDS=%e' -o /workspace/STEP.time /bin/bash -lc 'COMMAND' > /workspace/STEP.log 2>&1; rc=$?; cat /workspace/STEP.time; tail -n 14 /workspace/STEP.log; exit $rc. This saves full logs without exceeding output limits. Do not combine steps because each time must remain independent:
1. STEP=express-clone COMMAND=cd /workspace && git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/expressjs/express
2. STEP=express-install COMMAND=cd /workspace/express && npm install
3. STEP=express-test COMMAND=cd /workspace/express && npm test
4. STEP=rust-install COMMAND=curl --proto "=https" --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y --profile minimal
5. STEP=ripgrep-clone COMMAND=cd /workspace && git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep
6. STEP=ripgrep-build COMMAND=export PATH=/root/.cargo/bin:$PATH; cd /workspace/ripgrep && cargo build --release

Continue after a failed test, recording its exit code and reason. If installation/build fails, inspect the saved log and resource availability; recover only if a straightforward fix is possible, and time retries separately. If a command might exceed the exec timeout, launch it as a background job writing its exit status and poll every 30 seconds in another exec. Do not change npm scripts or source code, skip tests, reduce the requested release build, or claim completion while jobs are running. Finally run /workspace/ripgrep/target/release/rg --version, git -C /workspace/express rev-parse HEAD, git -C /workspace/ripgrep rev-parse HEAD, du -sb /workspace/ripgrep /workspace/ripgrep/target, and df -h /workspace. Leave the machine running and files intact. Report observed times, exit codes and any recovery; do not snapshot or sleep yet because the benchmark harness measures those next.

The working directory is /workspace. Node is preinstalled; if missing install it and record that separately.

Run each of the following as a SEPARATE computer exec call with timeoutMs 1200000 and argv ["/bin/bash","-lc", SHELL]. Use /usr/bin/time -f 'BENCH_WALL_SECONDS=%e' -o /workspace/STEP.time /bin/bash -lc 'COMMAND' > /workspace/STEP.log 2>&1; rc=$?; cat /workspace/STEP.time; tail -n 14 /workspace/STEP.log; exit $rc. Continue after a failed test, recording its exit code and reason. If installation/build fails, inspect the saved log and resource availability; recover only if a straightforward fix is possible, and time retries separately. If a command might exceed the exec timeout, launch it as a background job writing its exit status and poll every 30 seconds in another exec. Do not change npm scripts or source code, skip tests, reduce the requested release build, or claim completion while jobs are running. The working directory is /workspace. Node is preinstalled; if missing install it and record that separately.

Run each of the following as a SEPARATE computer exec call with timeoutMs 1200000 and argv ["/bin/bash","-lc", SHELL]. units.memoryUsageBytes: bytes for the entire V8 isolate

limitations: GraphQL data can arrive after the query. Empty rows and zero memory fields are retained, not treated as proof of zero consumption.
Memory describes the entire V8 isolate and can include multiple DOs. Filtering to one object does not make this a per-object heap measurement.
The interval contains every request to these prefixed resources, including setup and health checks. It is not attributed to one benchmark case.
Worker and DO datasets overlap in infrastructure scope; do not add their CPU or duration totals as a bill.
The Worker dataset has no DO namespace or object dimension. Its CPU and memory cannot substitute for missing caller-DO telemetry.
DO CPU time is actual CPU telemetry. DO billed compute uses duration in GB*s, not CPU time alone; analytics is not a final billing invoice.

caveats: Empty/missing/error telemetry is unknown, never zero. Available rows may be delayed or incomplete.
Metered Container values apply to each whole app and analytics window; multiple result files on one app are not individually attributable.

The allocation-time estimate assumes full nominal CPU and allocated RAM/disk for the entire start-to-observed-stop interval, including sleep. It is a planning estimate, not metered usage or an invoice. If no observed stop exists, its interval ends at the last saved event and does not bound subsequent running time.

Pass the latest result once per agent, plus separate failed agents. Duplicate agent snapshots disable model/allocation totals to avoid double counting. Manual diagnostic agents and gaps between saved runs are not covered by the allocation/model estimate; whole-app telemetry may include them.
Worker costs use only requests and CPU; DO costs use one namespace-level invocation and periodic dataset each. Script/object duplicate aggregates are excluded.
Model costs are SDK price estimates from saved usage, not provider billing receipts; failed requests may be missing usage.

Included allowances, minimum charges/rounding, contract discounts, logs, SQLite, egress, registry, retained snapshot storage and other unreported costs are excluded. Retained snapshot prices are unknown.

conservativeEnvelope.method: Full nominal CPU, RAM and disk from earliest agent start until final empty app inventory, including stopped periods. One envelope per app prevents overlapping Computer runs from double-counting. Excludes registry/snapshot storage, egress, logs, SQLite, plan allowances and billing rounding.
